title: ‘Show How 3M Is 0% at Fault:’ Expert Witness Used ChatGPT to Write Report Defending Company in Deadly Explosion Lawsuit

reading.body:
This incident shows a general-purpose conversational AI being used to produce a formal legal document, specifically an expert witness report, in a high-stakes civil lawsuit. The prompts entered by the expert witness explicitly directed the model to reach a predetermined conclusion, asking it to show that one party bore zero percent of the fault. That is a misuse of a tool outside the conditions it was built for, and it is also an example of a model being steered to assert a conclusion as analysis rather than deriving a conclusion from analysis.

The failure occurred at the point of human authorship, before the report entered the court record. An expert witness report is supposed to reflect independent professional judgment. Submitting one written to a predetermined instruction, by a general-purpose AI with no access to the physical evidence, witness accounts, or engineering data in the case, bypasses the professional check that expert testimony is meant to provide. The failure would have required scrutiny of the witness's drafting process to catch, and court discovery of the actual prompts is what surfaced it here.

It is not established that 3M directed or knew about the use of ChatGPT, that the report was formally admitted into evidence, or that any court has yet ruled on its admissibility or on the broader merits of the case.

reports.title: ‘Show How 3M Is 0% at Fault:’ Expert Witness Used ChatGPT to Write Report Defending Company in Deadly Explosion Lawsuit

summary:
An expert witness hired by 3M to defend the company in a lawsuit over a deadly Houston explosion used ChatGPT to write portions of his official report. Court documents reveal that the witness asked the AI tool to create an expert witness report showing that 3M was zero percent responsible for the 2020 Watson Grinding facility explosion, which killed three people and destroyed approximately 200 homes. The exposed prompts show how artificial intelligence was used to generate testimony in this high-stakes case involving hundreds of millions of dollars in potential liability.

The explosion resulted from a degraded rubber welding hose that leaked flammable gas. Dozens of homeowners sued 3M and Watson Grinding, claiming that 3M failed to properly maintain the facility's gas detection system and made other errors contributing to the disaster. This case demonstrates that AI is increasingly being used in courtroom proceedings, including expert witness testimony, and that the specific prompts used to create such reports can be discovered and made public during litigation, potentially damaging the credibility of the testimony.
